parts.latex:
In an opinion poll, $65\%$ of people indicated that they were in favour of an airport being built in a region near where they live.

If $5$ people were randomly chosen from those completing the poll, what is the probability that at least one person was not in favour of the airport being built?

solutions.latex:
The opposite of "at least one not in favour" is "all $5$ in favour".

Each person is in favour with probability $0.65$, independently.

$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{at least one not in favour}) &= 1-P(\text{all in favour}) \\ &= 1-0.65^5 \end{aligned}$$

Hence the answer is option A.
